en kassebon.explanation: "En kassebon" means "a register receipt". To tell a customer what to bring when exchanging something: "Husk din kassebon, når du bytter" (Remember your receipt when you exchange something).

related.en: a complaint about a faulty item

en kassedame.explanation: "En kassedame" means "a cashier". Literally it is "register lady", because "en dame" is a lady. To talk about a man or any person in the job, use "en kassemedarbejder" (a register employee): "Han er kassemedarbejder i et supermarked" (He is a cashier in a supermarket).

en kassemedarbejder.explanation: "En kassemedarbejder" means "a cashier". It is built from "kasse" (checkout) and "en medarbejder" (an employee), so it fits a man or a woman. To say you are applying for the job: "Hun søger job som kassemedarbejder" (She is applying for a job as a cashier).

en kasserolle.explanation: "En kasserolle" means "a saucepan". To say you cook something in it, use "i" (in): "Jeg koger ris i en kasserolle" (I cook rice in a saucepan).

en kastanje.explanation: "En kastanje" means "a chestnut". To name the kind you can roast and eat, use "ægte kastanjer" (sweet chestnuts): "Vi ristede ægte kastanjer" (We roasted sweet chestnuts). To name the kind that is not for eating, use "hestekastanjer" (horse chestnuts): "Man kan ikke spise hestekastanjer" (You cannot eat horse chestnuts).

en kat.explanation: "En kat" means "a cat". To say a cat purrs: "Katten spinder" (The cat purrs). To say you own one, keep "en": "Jeg har en kat" (I have a cat).

en katastrofe.explanation: "En katastrofe" means "a disaster". To say an event went very badly: "Festen var en katastrofe" (The party was a disaster). To name a flood or storm, put "natur" (nature) in front: "en naturkatastrofe" (a natural disaster).

en katedral.explanation: "En katedral" means "a cathedral". Danish also has the word "en domkirke" (a cathedral), as in "Roskilde Domkirke", where Danish kings and queens are buried.

en kategori.explanation: "En kategori" means "a category". To say you sort things into groups: "Vi deler ordene op i kategorier" (We divide the words into categories).

en kattebakke.explanation: "En kattebakke" means "a litter box". It is built from "kat" (cat) and "en bakke" (a tray). The word "bakke" also means "a hill", as in "Vi går op ad en bakke" (We walk up a hill).

en kaution.explanation: "En kaution" means "a bail payment". To say someone pays so they can wait outside prison, use "at stille kaution" (to put up bail): "Han stillede kaution" (He put up bail).

en kejser.explanation: "En kejser" means "an emperor". A woman in that role is "en kejserinde" (an empress): "Kejserinden bor i paladset" (The empress lives in the palace). The word is also in "et kejsersnit" (a C-section): "Hun fik et kejsersnit" (She had a C-section).

en kemiker.explanation: "En kemiker" means "a chemist". To say a chemist works in a lab: "Kemikeren arbejder i et laboratorium" (The chemist works in a laboratory). Do not use it for the shop worker who gives out medicine; that person is "en apoteker" (a pharmacist): "Jeg køber medicin hos apotekeren" (I buy medicine from the pharmacist).

en kendelse.explanation: "En kendelse" means "a ruling". To name the paper that lets police search a place, use "en retskendelse" (a court order): "Politiet har fået en retskendelse" (The police have got a court order).

en kerne.explanation: "En kerne" means "a core / kernel". To name the seeds inside a fruit, put the fruit in front: "æblekerner" (apple seeds). To name the center of an atom, use "en atomkerne" (an atomic nucleus).

en ketsjer.explanation: "En ketsjer" means "a racket". English speakers should note the spelling: it is "ketsjer", not "racket". To say you bring one to a game: "Jeg tager min ketsjer med til tennis" (I bring my racket to tennis).

en kidnapning.explanation: "En kidnapning" means "a kidnapping". The verb is "at kidnappe" (to kidnap): "De kidnappede ham" (They kidnapped him).

en kikkert.explanation: "En kikkert" means "a pair of binoculars". Danish has one word for it, so no "pair of" is needed: "Jeg har en kikkert" (I have a pair of binoculars).

en kiks.explanation: "En kiks" means "a biscuit". To talk about crackers with cheese: "kiks og ost" (crackers and cheese). To talk about sweet cookies, use "en småkage" (a cookie): "Hun bager småkager til jul" (She bakes cookies for Christmas).

en kilde.explanation: "En kilde" means "a source / spring". To ask where information comes from: "Hvad er din kilde?" (What is your source?) To talk about water coming out of the ground: "en kilde i bjergene" (a spring in the mountains).

en killing.explanation: "En killing" means "a kitten". To say there are several, the plural is "killinger": "Der er fire killinger i kurven" (There are four kittens in the basket).

en kilometer.explanation: "En kilometer" means "a kilometer". The plural stays the same: "ti kilometer" (ten kilometers). To give a speed, use "kilometer i timen" (kilometers per hour): "Bilen kører firs kilometer i timen" (The car drives eighty kilometers per hour).

en kind.explanation: "En kind" means "a cheek". To talk about both cheeks, the plural is "kinder": "Hendes kinder er røde" (Her cheeks are red).

en kineser.explanation: "En kineser" means "a Chinese person". It comes from "Kina" (China). For things from China, use "kinesisk" (Chinese): "kinesisk mad" (Chinese food).

en kiosk.explanation: "En kiosk" means "a kiosk / convenience store". To say you walk to one: "Jeg går ned til kiosken" (I walk down to the kiosk).
